encryption.label: Encryption
encryption.title: Locked, *every* step of the way
encryption.text: Your photos, videos, messages and medical information are encrypted when they are stored. Everything travels over an encrypted connection.

items.title: When it is stored
items.text: Photos, videos, messages and medical information are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, the standard banks and governments use. Each photo and video gets its own key.

items.title: When it travels
items.text: Everything between your phone and KINND is sent over an encrypted connection (TLS 1.3). Nobody on the network can read it.

items.title: Keys kept apart
items.text: The keys that unlock your data are stored apart from the data itself, in a separate, secured key vault. A copy of the data alone is unreadable.

protected.label: What is protected
protected.title: What is *protected*

oversight.label: What we can see
oversight.title: Built to keep *children* safe
oversight.text: Our management system watches for misuse around the clock. Every alarm is checked by a person on our team.

items.title: Family life stays private
items.text: In normal use, nobody at KINND sees your photos, messages or your child's information. Our system works on technical signals only.

items.title: When an alarm goes off
items.text: If activity sets off an alarm, our team first sees masked technical details of that case: sign-ins, devices, IP addresses and the warnings that fired. If there are grounds to look further, we follow the protocols of the Danish police's cyber crime centre (NC3), and a second senior reviewer checks the case before it is escalated.

items.title: Every look is logged
items.text: Every time an employee views details in a case, it is logged and audited. That audit log goes into the report we hand to the authorities.

abuse.label: Abuse and fraud
abuse.title: How we catch *abuse* and fraud
abuse.text: Abuse Central, our warning engine, works on technical signals only. When something looks wrong, a person on our team looks into it.

items.title: Warnings that catch misuse early
items.text: Abuse Central uses a wide set of triggers and patterns to spot signs of misuse: unusual sign-ins, accounts created to reach a child, and attempts to get access someone should not have.

items.title: Reports from you
items.text: Worried about an account? Write to abuse@kinnd.eu. Every report gets a case that a person follows to the end. In the app, parents can remove a family member at any time.

items.title: We work with the authorities
items.text: Confirmed illegal cases are handed to the police with the information they need, including the audit log of who viewed what. We follow each case until it is closed.

items.title: We stay out of family conflicts
items.text: KINND is a private space to share in. We do not take sides or settle disagreements.
